research_question: On genuinely disjoint MS MARCO training queries whose positives occur in the existing frozen 1M corpus, can one closed-form, PCA-anchored cutoff-weighted update of a rank-64 RPQ codebook improve Recall@10 over the storage-identical unsupervised rank-64 RPQ baseline without fold, seed, MRR, nDCG, payload, or centroid-drift failure?
scope: fresh-query method development only; no old holdout reuse, independent confirmation, official MS MARCO score, ScaNN claim, SOTA claim, or production-kernel claim

parent_evidence.interpretation: V11 outcomes are disclosed design motivation only. The V12 executable accepts no V11 packet path and refits both baseline and challenger within every fresh-data training fold.

evidence_boundary.allowed_claim: the preregistered anchored cutoff-aware centroid update did or did not show stable out-of-fold advantage over its storage-identical unsupervised rank-64 RPQ initializer on the frozen 1M-corpus restricted development task
forbidden_claims: official MS MARCO development or leaderboard performance
generalization beyond the frozen 1M restricted corpus

fresh_query_freeze.source_dataset: MS MARCO passage ranking v1 training queries and qrels
fresh_query_freeze.selection_rule: among train qids with text and at least one positive passage id in the exact frozen 1M doc-id array, exclude every qid in the three historical 6,980-query split files, sort by SHA256('rars_v12_fresh_train_selection_v1\0' || canonical_qid_utf8), and take the first 2,500
fresh_query_freeze.relevance_denominator: all positive qrels for that query whose passage id occurs in the frozen 1M corpus

method.basis: one deterministic uncentred PCA rank-64 basis fit only on candidate residual rows reached by the four training folds; the held-out fold contributes no basis, codebook, pair, weight, or hyperparameter information
method.baseline: Faiss ProductQuantizer fit without labels on the same fold-training coefficients, seed, iterations, and payload
method.challenger: one cutoff-weighted closed-form centroid update with the baseline assignments frozen during the update, followed by ordinary nearest-centroid re-encoding

cutoff_pair_mining.promotion: known positive at Base ranks 11..40 versus an unjudged Base Top-10 challenger when same-candidate exact prefers the positive
cutoff_pair_mining.protection: known positive in Base Top-10 versus an unjudged rank 11..26 challenger when same-candidate exact prefers the positive

cutoff_weighting.block_sensitivity: squared L2 norm of the PCA-projected query within each four-dimensional RPQ block, normalized to sum to one per pair
cutoff_weighting.documents_receiving_pair_mass: both the known-positive and unjudged-challenger residual rows
cutoff_weighting.normalization: within each block, active residual rows receive mean additive boost eight before clipping

centroid_update.empty_cell_policy: remain byte-identical to the unsupervised centroid
centroid_update.objective: weighted within-cell coefficient squared error plus anchor_pseudocount times squared centroid drift

rpq_training.implementation: Faiss ProductQuantizer on fixed PCA coefficients

prohibited_actions: reading a V9, V10, or V11 result packet from the V12 freezer or trainer
using any of the historical 6,980 MS MARCO dev qids
using the held-out fold to fit PCA, RPQ, cutoff pairs, weights, centroids, alpha, Top-B, or gates
changing the method, weights, drift radius, seed list, or decision thresholds after outcomes appear
selecting the best seed or fold
calling an unjudged challenger explicitly non-relevant
claiming official MS MARCO performance from the restricted 1M corpus
claiming production efficiency from the Python development evaluator
